title: Exam 1
subtitle: Pediatric Health Promotion & Respiratory Alterations

practiceExams.note: The study guide lists 44 topic questions (their points add up to exactly 44), 2 alternate-format items, and 5 dosage calculations, and gives no time limit. Practice exams use the 44 topic questions in the study guide's exact proportions plus the 5 dosage calculations (49 total), timed at 54 minutes.

outcomes: Assess biological development and behaviors from infancy through adolescence
Promote health and prevent disease and injury at each developmental stage
Recognize unexpected findings and the health concerns they signal
Apply the vaccine schedule and atraumatic care during immunization
Recognize respiratory distress in children and prioritize airway, breathing, and circulation
Explain etiology, presentation, diagnosis, and treatment of pediatric respiratory alterations
Apply the nursing process using clinical judgment functions with pediatric clients and families
Calculate safe, weight-based pediatric medication doses

objectives.title: Health Promotion Across Childhood
items: Assess and discuss biological development for newborn, infant, toddler, preschool, school-age, and adolescent clients
Assess and discuss behaviors at each developmental stage
Examine health promotion and prevention of disease and injury at each stage
Discuss health concerns related to unexpected findings
Discuss the vaccine schedule and the nurse's role in vaccine administration and infection control

objectives.title: Respiratory Alterations
items: Examine the anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, and screening of pediatric clients with alterations in respiratory function
Explore etiology, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and treatment
Describe the effect of respiratory alterations on the child's overall health
Explore the role of the nurse caring for these children
Apply the nursing process using clinical judgment functions
